contracts: Selectors 0xAB and 0x50 create Type-0x44 actors with the shared zero template, Type-0x44 animation, and actor flag initialization; selector 0xAB additionally requires INTERACTION_GATE_TYPE44.
Selector 0x8E creates the Type-0x5A template, while selectors 0x90 and 0x91 reuse it and publish runtime types 0x5C and 0x5D.
Selectors 0xBB and 0xA9 reverse-spawn the Type-0x4E template, with selector 0xBB forcing the facing byte to 0xFF; selector 0xA6 reverse-spawns the Type-0x4F template.
Selector 0x17 creates the Type-0x53 template and applies the exact (+0x18,-0x0E) actor position offset.
Selector 0x30 creates the Type-0x84 level-event template and applies the exact +0x0C actor Y offset.
evidence: Existing actor-template, Type-0x44, and Type-0x52/0x53 static contracts
limitations: No user-facing object identity is claimed for these runtime types or template-derived actors.
The canonical names preserve selector/override distinctions because the wrappers have materially different gates or mutations.
conclusion: The remaining compact late interaction wrappers now have stable creation identities tied to their exact templates, selectors, gates, and post-allocation mutations.
